identity.title: Pericardial friction rub (triphasic scratchy sound, LSB, leaning forward, end-expiration)

technique.how: Sit the patient forward, ask for full exhalation and a breath-hold, and listen with the diaphragm firmly at the left lower sternal border. A rub is a superficial scratchy or leathery sound, classically with up to three components (atrial systole, ventricular systole, early diastole); it may come and go, so re-auscultate several times over hours.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room; patient able to sit forward and hold expiration.

interpretation.positive_finding: A rub is one of the four ESC diagnostic criteria for acute pericarditis (chest pain, rub, ECG changes, new/worsening effusion; 2 of 4 required) and is regarded as highly specific, but no sensitivity/specificity against an independent reference standard was found.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of a rub does not exclude pericarditis; rubs are intermittent and were not present in most patients in prospective pericarditis cohorts. Absence of a rub with a large effusion says nothing about tamponade.
interpretation.pitfalls: Pleural rubs (disappear with breath-hold) and crunching artefact from skin or hair mimic a pericardial rub. The rub often vanishes as effusion accumulates, so its disappearance may signal worsening rather than improvement.
interpretation.changes_what: Rub present: treat as pericarditis criterion; get ECG, troponin, echo. Rub absent: still apply the other three criteria; do not use to discount pericarditis or tamponade.

sources.citation: Adler Y, Charron P, Imazio M, Badano L, Barón-Esquivias G, Bogaert J, Brucato A, Gueret P, et al. 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases. Eur Heart J. 2015;36(42):2921-2964.

Imazio M, Brucato A, Barbieri A, Ferroni F, Maestroni S, Ligabue G, Chinaglia A, Cumetti D, et al. Good prognosis for pericarditis with and without myocardial involvement: results from a multicenter, prospective cohort study. Circulation. 2013;128(1):42-49.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use presence or absence of a rub to decide about tamponade; that decision rests on hemodynamics, pulsus paradoxus, JVP and echo.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rub with hypotension, rising JVP, or pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg means possible tamponade: urgent echo and cardiology.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data found; rub is intermittent and examiner-dependent.

extraction_notes: Searches: 'pericardial friction rub acute pericarditis' (10 recent hits, none diagnostic-accuracy), 'Imazio pericarditis ... prognosis' and 'acute pericarditis day-hospital' (PMIDs 23709669, 15028364 fetched). No study reporting sensitivity/specificity or LR of a rub against an independent reference standard was found; the rub is itself one of the four ESC diagnostic criteria (quote from PMID 23709669 abstract: 'The diagnosis of acute pericarditis was based on the presence of 2 of 4 clinical criteria (chest pain, pericardial rubs, widespread ST-segment elevation or PR depression, and new or worsening pericardial effusion)'), so any accuracy estimate would be circular (incorporation bias). Rub frequency in pericarditis cohorts is reported in full texts I could not access (Circulation 2013 and JACC 2004 not in PMC), so no prevalence-of-sign number is entered. ESC 2015 guideline (PMID 26320112) has no PubMed abstract; its criteria are cited from the guideline document itself as consensus. Status not_quantified as expected for this priority-2 id.
